worries.worry: Money is tight for us. Seedlings and tools sound dear.
answers: We can share ours. Cuttings cost almost nothing.
The park got new benches last spring.
There is always money for what matters.
worries.right_reply: Shared tools, then. That we can do.
worries.wrong_reply: Perhaps. We will see how spring goes.

worries.worry: It is one small street. Would it truly change anything?
answers: Streets copy the street next door. Ours can start it.
Two streets over, they repainted their fences.
If nobody starts, nobody ever will.
worries.right_reply: If it spreads... all right. We will try.
worries.wrong_reply: Maybe so. It still feels small to us.

worries.worry: We are not young now. Digging and lifting is too much.
answers: We will take the heavy parts. You could water the pots.
The soil on this street is soft and light.
A little garden work would do you good.
worries.right_reply: Watering we can manage. Thank you.
worries.wrong_reply: We will watch from the window for now.

worries.worry: We live far from the sea. Let the shore streets worry.
answers: Storms reach further inland now. The bay holds us all.
The shore streets do get the worst of it.
Everyone must do their part, near or far.
worries.right_reply: The whole bay... we had not thought of that.
worries.wrong_reply: Far is far. But we will think on it.

worries.worry: Diggers and mud for weeks? We just redid our front path.
answers: One corner at a time, and we keep your path clear.
The children here love watching the diggers.
A little mud never hurt anyone.
worries.right_reply: Keep the path clear, and we are easy.
worries.wrong_reply: Let us hope the mud settles quickly.

worries.worry: We signed a petition once. Nothing came of it.
answers: Come watch the first day. You will see it with your own eyes.
The new drain covers do look sturdy.
You cannot give up after one try.
worries.right_reply: Seeing is believing. We will come by.
worries.wrong_reply: Words are easy. We have heard many.
